name: Slack
use_case: read channel history and post messages in customers' Slack workspaces

verdict.label: Hard · weeks of waiting
verdict.summary: Creating the app takes minutes, and it can be installed in other workspaces right away. But commercially distributed apps outside the Slack Marketplace get throttled history APIs (1 request per minute), and getting listed takes 10 active installs plus a review of up to about 12 weeks.
verdict.active_effort: 1–2 hours to set up; 1–2 days to prepare a Marketplace submission
verdict.wait: Up to 10 business days (preliminary) plus up to 10 weeks (functional review)
verdict.gating_step: Slack Marketplace review: needed to escape the non-Marketplace rate limits and to distribute commercially under Slack's API terms

concept: A Slack app is created at api.slack.com/apps against one development workspace. Turning on public distribution lets other workspaces install it via OAuth. Each install gives your integration a bot and/or user token for that workspace. Whether the app is Marketplace-approved changes which rate limits those tokens get.

paths.name: Internal app (your own workspace only)
paths.when: Internal tools. Internal customer-built apps keep the normal rate limits.

paths.name: Distributed but unlisted
paths.when: Works for pilots, but new installs get conversations.history and conversations.replies at 1 request per minute and 15 objects per call. Slack's terms say the Marketplace is the channel for commercial distribution.

paths.name: Slack Marketplace
paths.when: Commercial agents that read conversations at any real volume.

composio.managed_note: Composio's Slack toolkit lists a Composio-managed OAuth app. Composio's FAQ also covers the “This app isn't listed in the Slack Marketplace” warning users may see.
when_own_app: Production: users should see your app name on the consent screen, not “Composio”.
You need scopes beyond Composio's defaults.
You need your own rate-limit quota (managed apps share quota across Composio users).
You need faster polling triggers than the managed 15-minute minimum.
Self-hosted or regional instances of the provider.

stages.name: Build & test (works today)
stages.summary: Self-serve. Once public distribution is on, any workspace can install the app; nobody has to approve it first.

limits.text: For commercially distributed apps not approved for the Marketplace, conversations.history is limited to 1 request per minute, and the maximum and default page size drops to 15 messages. Applies to apps created after May 29, 2025, and to new installs of older apps.
Existing installs of unlisted apps were also moved to the new limits on March 3, 2026.

steps.title: Create the app at api.slack.com/apps
steps.detail: “Create New App” → “From scratch” (or from a manifest), and pick a development workspace.

steps.title: Add the redirect URL
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs → add Composio's callback URL → Save.

steps.title: Choose bot and user token scopes
steps.detail: List the API methods your agent calls and add only the scopes those methods need. Prefer bot tokens unless the agent must act as a specific person.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution → complete the checklist → Activate. This is required before other workspaces can install the app, and before any Marketplace submission.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from Basic Information into Composio.

steps.title: Install into a second, non-dev workspace
steps.detail: Slack's reviewers test as a brand-new customer would, so you should too, including uninstalling.

stages.name: Go to production (Slack Marketplace)
stages.summary: Two review phases. Budget the calendar time, because Slack says it can't speed reviews up to match your launch.

limits.text: You can't submit until the app is installed on 10 or more active workspaces (used in the past 28 days).

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspace installs
steps.detail: Pilot customers count. Plan for this; it happens while you're still on the unlisted rate limits.

steps.title: Remove scopes for features you haven't built
steps.detail: Slack only approves scopes it can see in use, and won't accept legacy or broad scopes like admin.*, search:read, read, post or identity.*.

steps.title: Prepare reviewer access and a demo video
steps.detail: Provide test credentials for your service (a long trial if paid) and a video of install, OAuth, setup, usage and uninstall.

steps.title: Submit from “Submit to Slack Marketplace”
steps.detail: Automated checks run first. The preliminary review takes up to 10 business days, and each resubmission in this phase puts you back at the end of the queue.

steps.title: Pass the functional review
steps.detail: Up to 10 weeks for new apps. Resubmitting during this phase doesn't reset your place.

steps.title: Publish when you choose
steps.detail: After approval, the live config is locked. Future scope or redirect changes need another review, and staging copies help.

requirements.detail: Required for other workspaces to install the app, and before a Marketplace submission.
Active means used in the past 28 days.

requirements.item: Reviewer test account plus demo video
requirements.detail: Reviewers can't access your Slack workspaces; they install the app themselves.

gotchas.title: History APIs crawl until you're listed
gotchas.detail: 1 request per minute with 15 messages per page makes agents that read channel context painfully slow for new installs. Internal apps are exempt.

gotchas.title: Chicken-and-egg: 10 installs before review
gotchas.detail: You need 10 active workspaces while still on the throttled unlisted tier, so plan pilots around it.

gotchas.title: Preliminary resubmissions reset the queue
gotchas.detail: Sloppy listing copy costs you full waits. Get links, descriptions and scope reasons right the first time.

gotchas.title: Published config is frozen
gotchas.detail: Adding a scope later means another review of up to 6 weeks for updates. Keep a staging app built from the same manifest.

gotchas.title: Customer admins may require app approval
gotchas.detail: In workspaces that restrict apps, users submit a request instead of installing, and Slack shows a warning for unlisted apps.

blockers.cause: The app is commercially distributed but not Marketplace-approved (Tier 1: 1 request per minute, limit 15).
blockers.fix: Back off using Retry-After, cache history, and get listed. Internal apps aren't affected.

blockers.cause: The callback URL isn't saved under OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs.
blockers.fix: Add Composio's callback URL exactly and click Save URLs.

blockers.cause: The workspace requires admin approval for apps.
blockers.fix: Ask the workspace admin to approve the app in their app management settings.

Generate an app manifest for dev and staging copies
